title: Response envelope padding causes parse attribute misalignment for proxied tool responses (Private/Dedicated)
creator: Evan Park
description: Several customers running Private and Dedicated deployments have reported intermittent corruption of structured tool-invocation parsing when responses are proxied through certain gateway images. The runtime returns a correct JSON tool-call envelope, but an extra padding segment appended by upstream proxies causes our structured-output reassembler to introduce an empty attribute token which shifts subsequent fields and results in incorrect tool parameters being executed. This has manifested as customer-visible wrong-argument tool invocations and a small number of high-severity escalations. Hosted API customers are rarely affected (the issue depends on an older proxy behavior seen in some Private/Dedicated gateway versions).
environment: Private / Dedicated (observed on proxy image v3.4.1 and custom edge bundlers). Staging reproducer available. Noticed with streaming and chunked multipart responses when proxies append alignment padding to the response body.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a Private runtime with gateway image v3.4.1 or configure a dedicated proxy that appends 8KB alignment padding to responses.
2) Send a streaming tool-invoke request via the /invoke endpoint with a tool payload that includes nested structured fields (example: pdf_extractor with positional args and metadata).
3) Observe that the runtime emits a correct JSON envelope with a trailing JSON close brace, followed by non-JSON padding bytes (0x00 or repeated spaces).

4) The parser in the reassembly layer treats padding as an extra token during boundary trimming, emitting an empty attribute which causes the mapping step to shift subsequent attributes left (e.g., name->namespace, param0->name).
5) Confirm by capturing raw TCP stream at edge and running the attach-parser test harness which shows the attribute index mismatch.
impact: High — production customers have reported incorrect tool executions leading to data-processing errors. Affected customers include two enterprise Private deployments and one Dedicated customer with high request volume. Customer impact classification: high.
mitigation: Short-term mitigation pushed: configuration flag on affected gateway images to disable response padding. Workaround instructions sent to customers (upgrade proxy or set REDWOOD_PROXY_STRIP_PADDING=true). We also rolled a temporary server-side tolerant-mode that trims trailing NUL bytes for canary customers.
root_cause_hypothesis: Upstream proxy/bundler added deterministic padding for MTU/edge-storage alignment. Our reassembly code assumed only whitespace could appear after the JSON envelope and used a brittle delimiter-trim algorithm that incorrectly converts certain padding patterns into zero-length attributes when merging chunks.
proposed_fix: 1) Update chunk reassembly module to explicitly detect JSON envelope termination and ignore any padding bytes that occur after the closing '}' or ']' up to a configurable limit (default 1KB). 2) Harden the structured-output mapper to validate attribute count against schema before applying positional mappings; if mismatch, raise a parse error and trigger fallback. 3) Add end-to-end tests (unit + integration) covering padded responses, base64 attachments, and edge cases where padding contains valid whitespace. 4) Release fix in runtime-1.19 and backport a minimal sanitizer patch to runtime-1.18 for immediate deployment. 5) Publish a proxy config patch that strips padding at the edge (recommended for Private/Dedicated customers).
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests added and green in CI covering padded responses and streaming multipart tool calls.
Canary rollout to 10% of Dedicated capacity with no new parse errors for 48 hours.
Affected Private customers moved to patched gateway or had proxy config applied; no new escalations for 7 days post-rollout.
Telemetry updated to surface parse-mismatch events and attribute-shift rate; alert configured for >1% regression over baseline.
Patch released on runtime-1.19 and minimal sanitizer backport on runtime-1.18 deployed to staging and then production per rollout plan.
